# #407 — SHAPE-7: When does the rename happen, and does the archaeology survive a squash?

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: question, memory

Parent: #400. **Question, not work. Do not implement.**

## Decided 2026-07-24

Keep the name **open-brain locally** until the design is vetted, then rename —
likely with some squashed older commits — and launch publicly as **code-brain** or
similar.

Rationale: there are **at least 9000 projects named open-brain**, so the current
name was never going to be findable and there is no rename tax worth deferring
for. This repo is public with 4 stars — nobody is watching, so the rename costs
nothing today and costs more every month it waits.

Standing preference on record: *would rather have a FOSS app with 100k stars than
a patent.*

## Counter-considerations recorded

- cognee, mem0, Zep and Graphiti are all **invented words**. Descriptive names
  lose to noise; invented ones can be owned.
- The name should point at the **interesting half** — drift, intent, conformance —
  rather than the commodity half (memory for coding agents), where four projects
  already compete. `code-brain` arguably names the commodity half.
- Working hook line: **"your issues are closed. Is any of it running?"** That is
  the pitch, and the name should not fight it.

## Question 1 — what is the actual trigger?

"After vetting" is not a condition anything can test. Candidate triggers, from
weakest to strongest:

- the panel (#406) returns GO
- R1/R2/R3 are landed and one assertion has caught a real drift **in production**
- someone other than Rico runs it successfully

The middle one is the honest bar: the differentiator has to have **worked once**
before it goes in the name. The PreCompact fix already set this precedent — it
was claimed only after it fired in production on a real compaction.

## Question 2 — does the archaeology survive a squash?

**This is the one with real risk.** The most compelling thing about the project is
the record: **sixteen capabilities built, eight of them never wired**, measured
and documented rather than asserted. From `docs/code-brain-design.md`:

> Every sprint issue closed. Every PR merged, CI green, review swarms run. The
> issues closed against code that **exists** while nobody checked whether anything
> **runs**.

That is the origin story, and it only lands **because it is real**. A squash that
erases the commits erases the proof, leaving a claim that reads like marketing.

Constraint to carry into any rename plan: **`docs/code-brain-design.md` must
survive the squash**, and so should the issue history — #386-#399 plus this epic
are part of the evidence, not clutter. Squashing code commits is fine; squashing
the record is self-defeating.

## Question 3 — one name or two?

If #SHAPE-1 resolves to two products, this needs **two** names, and `code-brain`
may be the wrong one for either. Do not name before that fork is resolved.

## What would settle it

Pick the trigger from Question 1 and write it down as a testable condition. Then
the rename becomes a scheduled consequence rather than a recurring debate.

## Depends on

#SHAPE-1 (one product or two), #SHAPE-6 (panel result).
